testcase.name: a workspace-only change on a channel participant is a typed remap, never identical
a workspace-only change on a project member is a typed remap, never identical
a workspace-only change on the active execution attempt is a conflicting owner, never identical
a record filed under the wrong family section is quarantined before comparison, never compared
a section without truncation evidence is rejected, never read as complete
a null record is quarantined and the comparison can never be identical
a section over its declared limit or the record cap is a typed limit violation
an output beyond the findings bound is rejected with a typed limit violation
arbitrary text in a digest field never surfaces; only the opaque reference is emitted
an ill-formed identifier drift is reported through opaque references only
malformed-record fingerprints are canonical: object key order cannot change the outcome
conflicting duplicate records are quarantined deterministically regardless of input order
identical snapshots of every known domain yield an identical verdict with zero findings
a declared-empty section is a proven fact, not an unknown domain
a record present before and absent after is a missing record
a non-grant record only present after is unexpected; a new grant row is widened access
the same stable id twice within one section is a duplicated record on that side
an auth identity resolving to a different user is a remapped record
digest drift is reported for content refs and event history independently
access growth is widened access; access narrowing is an attribute change, never widened
a channel widened from participants to workspace visibility is widened access
a regressed read frontier is lost read state, per channel and per thread
a read frontier that only advanced is an attribute change, not lost state
the active execution attempt bound to another owner is a conflicting attempt owner
owner drift on a superseded attempt is an attribute change, and a new active attempt is unexpected
other determinate drift on a matched record is a changed attribute
reordered equivalent records produce byte-identical results
repeated runs over the same input are byte-stable and carry no timestamps
mismatched snapshot identity is a typed error, not a diff
malformed snapshot identity is a typed error
a truncated section is flagged on each side and can never read as a clean scan
a missing family section is an unknown domain, never zero and never per-record missing
a family section absent from both sides is one unknown-domain finding for both
ambiguous audience records are quarantined, excluded from matching, and never a success
a malformed record is quarantined as malformed with the offending field named
determinate findings dominate the verdict even when the input is also incomplete
output is sanitized: allow-listed detail keys only, and input extras never surface
